claims.text: Headline: Japan shakes
claims.note: Reuters (via The Star), citing NHK: magnitude 5 quake in Nagano on 18 April. Headline is figurative and joins two stories.

claims.text: Headline: Iran cuts deals on who gets through Hormuz
claims.note: Ahram Online: Iran announced conditional reopening (designated route, IRGC permission). 'Cuts deals' is not in the source; reworded.

claims.text: Subheadline: someone always pays the toll
claims.note: Rhetorical line.

claims.text: Earthquake hit Nagano Prefecture at 2:54 PM local time, magnitude 5.0
claims.note: JMA: Mj5.0 at 13:20 JST on 18 April, depth 10 km. A second quake followed at about 14:54 JST (https://earthquaketrack.com/quakes/2026-04-18-05-54-30-utc-4-9-10). The time and magnitude are combined from two different events.

claims.text: Quake suspended the Shinanogawa Limited Express and shut the Shinonoi Line between Matsumoto and Nagano; four trains canceled; JR delays hours later
claims.note: No report found of these suspensions after two searches (only a brief Hokuriku Shinkansen disruption at Nagano Station mentioned by one low-grade source). 'Shinanogawa Limited Express' does not appear to be a real service name; JR's is 'Shinano'.

claims.text: No tsunami warning
claims.note: Inland quake; no tsunami risk reported. Not kept in copy (not needed).

claims.text: Passengers stranded between cities while aftershocks rattle the infrastructure; thousands of commuters checking phones
claims.note: Invented scene.

claims.text: Iran announced the Strait of Hormuz is 'open' but with conditions
claims.note: Ahram Online: open for the rest of the ceasefire via a designated route with prior IRGC permission. BBC (via The Star Kenya) quotes Araghchi: passage 'declared completely open'.

claims.text: Not the traditional toll, but fees to 'secure' the waterway
claims.note: No 17-18 April report of Iranian fees found. The Iran ambassador's remarks on fees for 'services' (Baird Maritime/Reuters) date from 8 June 2026.

claims.text: Hormuz carries 21% of global petroleum liquids
claims.note: EIA: about 21% of global petroleum liquids consumption (2018); about one-fifth in 2024. Pre-war baseline, not a current flow; not kept.

claims.text: US blockade first hit Iranian ports five days ago
claims.note: Blockade began 13 April 2026, five days before the edition.

claims.text: The BBC reports crude falling as markets digest Iran's ceasefire posturing
claims.note: BBC News story syndicated by The Star (Kenya): Brent fell to $88 from above $98 earlier on 17 April after Iran said the strait was open.

claims.text: Oil prices down from the panic peaks
claims.note: BBC: Brent peaked above $119 in March.

claims.text: US extended its waiver for sanctioned Russian oil purchases
claims.note: Al-Monitor (AFP): Treasury issued a month-long waiver on 17 April for Russian oil already loaded on vessels, valid to 16 May.

claims.text: Day 50 of the US-Iran conflict
claims.note: Syndicated Al Jazeera explainer dated 18 April 2026: 'What is happening on day 50 of the US-Iran conflict?'

claims.text: Al Jazeera's coverage suggests this is more about managing energy markets than resolving anything
claims.note: Characterisation not found in Al Jazeera coverage.

claims.text: Starmer faces calls to resign over the Peter Mandelson vetting scandal
claims.note: AP (via Boston.com), 16 April: government admitted Mandelson failed vetting before becoming US ambassador; Starmer faced calls to resign.

claims.text: The scandal started as insider gossip about inappropriate appointments
claims.note: Not in any report.

claims.text: Times of India reports growing resignation calls over what they call 'Mandelson's nightmare'
claims.note: TOI did report resignation calls (https://www.inkl.com/news/mandelson-vetting-storm-why-uk-pm-starmer-is-under-fire-can-he-be-ousted), but the 'Mandelson nightmare' phrase is from an AP analysis (https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/04/19/uk-pms-mandelson-nightmare-never-ends-it-may-now-cost-him-his-job/), not TOI. Copy attributes to AP.

claims.text: Even Starmer's own backbenchers won't publicly support the appointment
claims.note: Not sourced.

claims.text: Global sentiment 61/100, Bitcoin sentiment 70, Ethereum 69, conflict and security 55, market signal 56
claims.note: internal feed metric, not reportable

claims.text: SCMP reports on Hong Kong's ambitions to become a global gold vault
claims.note: SCMP: 'Hong Kong wants to become a global gold vault. Does the Iran war create an opening?'

claims.text: Chinese robo-diving suit helps users consume 40% less oxygen
claims.note: SCMP: 'could help users consume almost 40% less oxygen'; Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology. Military insinuation removed.

claims.text: Mitsune's KEXP performance
claims.note: playlist/video pick, not news

edits.headline: Iran says Strait of Hormuz is open for rest of ceasefire
edits.subheadline: Brent crude fell to $88 a barrel after Iran's foreign minister said the strait was open to commercial ships, BBC News reported.
editorialBody: Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said passage for all commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz was "completely open" for the rest of the ceasefire, BBC News reported. Brent crude fell to $88 a barrel on 17 April, from above $98 earlier that day, the BBC said.

Iran said ships would need to follow a designated route and get prior permission from the Revolutionary Guards, Ahram Online reported. President Trump said the US naval blockade of Iranian ports would continue until a final deal was reached, Ahram Online said.
The US Treasury issued a month-long waiver for purchases of Russian oil already loaded on ships, Al-Monitor reported.
In the UK, Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced calls to resign after the government said Peter Mandelson had failed security vetting before becoming ambassador to the US, the Associated Press reported.
An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5 struck Nagano Prefecture in central Japan on 18 April, Reuters reported, citing NHK.

Hong Kong is seeking to become a global gold storage hub, the South China Morning Post reported. Researchers in Shenzhen built a robotic diving suit that could help users consume almost 40% less oxygen, the SCMP reported.
